description: Change of use of basement from Nightclub (Use Class Sui Generis) to Class E, including internal subdivision into individual units and replacement of entrance door on front elevation and installation of an automatic opening vent (AOV) to the rear.
decision_conditions: <p><span id="docs-internal-guid-ade8b4c6-7fff-5d4a-e9f0-5c7a95b4d9ad"><span style="font-size: 11pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">Insufficient information has been provided to demonstrate that the proposed development would not result in harm to the significance of the Grade II listed building. The proposal would, therefore, fail to comply with Policy HC1 of the London Plan and Policy LP3 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (2020).</span></span></p>

<p><span id="docs-internal-guid-f81e3796-7fff-117d-7a12-836e0ea391e5"><span style="font-size: 11pt; font-family: Arial, sans-serif; background-color: transparent; font-variant-numeric: normal; font-variant-east-asian: normal; font-variant-alternates: normal; font-variant-position: normal; font-variant-emoji: normal; vertical-align: baseline; white-space-collapse: preserve;">The proposed office floorspace (Class E), by reason of its subterranean basement location, would fail to provide a high-quality or sustainable working environment. The units would be characterised by a significant lack of natural daylight, a total absence of external outlook, and inadequate natural ventilation, resulting in an oppressive sense of enclosure and a poor standard of amenity for future occupiers. Consequently, the proposal is contrary to Policy E1 of the London Plan (2021) and Policies LP26 and LP27 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033 (LP33), which require new employment floorspace to be well-designed, functional, and conducive to the well-being of its users.</span></span></p>

<p>By reason of the loss of the existing nightclub use, the loss of this night-time economy use would undermine the vitality and vibrancy of the Dalston Major Town Centre, adversely impacting local footfall and the diversity of the visitor experience. Furthermore, the applicant has failed to provide robust evidence to demonstrate that the use is no longer viable or that its removal is necessary to protect local amenity. The development is therefore contrary to Policy HC6 of the London Plan (2021), Policy LP38 of the Hackney Local Plan 2033, and Objectives 4 and 6 of the Dalston Plan SPD (2025), which collectively seek to protect, support, and promote Dalston’s night-time economy.</p>
